title: Color in a Jar - Volume One
summary: Color in a Jar: The West is the first volume of Christian's AI-made coloring book, where every page holds a small world inside a jar. This Note walks through ten of those worlds, from an oasis and a peach orchard to the deep sea and the polar jar, each shown in color, in black and white, and in a companion scene with GlazyArray, Robot Marley and A.L.T.A. The book is on Amazon in print and digital, with Volume Two on the way.

post.title: Color in a Jar: The West
post.body:
This is Color in a Jar: The West, the first volume of Color in a Jar: coloring pages where every scene lives inside glass. Its full title on Amazon is Color in a Jar: The West: A 50 States Coloring Book, Nevada, California, Utah, Oregon & Idaho.

## How it was made

Every page was generated with AI, using a process I spent months refining and polishing. I built the prompts with help from a tool of my own, which you can read about here: https://www.christiangehrke.com/?workshop+winter+day+propre-engine

## How the sections work

Each section below is one world from the book. The companion scene runs across the top, and underneath it the page itself sits side by side, in color and in black and white. The companion scenes aren't in the book; I made them to introduce it, with the Field Notes narrators stepping into each world: GlazyArray, the brass robot, Robot Marley, and A.L.T.A. Marley gets a new hat in nearly every world. The colored pages were made with AI, and they're only suggestions; the colors are up to whoever is holding the pencils. What I love about this book is how much is going on: worlds within worlds, and a lot of color waiting to happen.

## More in the book

There's more inside than these sections: a walled garden, a lily pond, a snowy Alpine Adventure village, a savanna, a bamboo grove, a bell jar of mushrooms and ferns, a greenhouse, and a bowl of succulents with a string of pearls spilling over the rim and a lizard on a rock.

## Where to find it

Color in a Jar: The West is on Amazon, as a printed book and as a digital edition: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H1QG4NX7

Volume Two is planned, but it isn't published yet.

The jar is the frame. Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

episode.title: Worlds in a jar
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

This Note came without a trail, a tracker or a single mile. It came in a jar.

Color in a Jar, The West, is the first volume of a coloring book, and every page in it puts a whole world behind glass. Every page was made with AI, through a process Christian spent months refining, with prompts built in a tool of his own. That kind of patience doesn't show on the page. What shows is how easy it all looks.

On this Note, the book comes as ten worlds. Each one arrives three ways. The page in clean black lines, the same page filled in with color, and a bigger scene that steps outside the glass.

***

Take the peach orchard. On the page, a mason jar stands on a wooden porch rail. Inside it, a peach tree hangs heavy with fruit, bees drift around an empty crate, and the grass grows right up to the glass. Outside the jar, past the rail, there's a red barn, a farmhouse with a porch of its own, and soft hills. A world inside a world, sitting on the edge of another one. There's a lot to color there, leaf by leaf.

The jungle jar has a clip top and rests on a mossy log. A toucan sits on a branch, a sloth hangs from a vine near the top, and a waterfall pours down behind the big green leaves and ferns. A few tiny mushrooms have settled on the log outside, as if they'd like to get in.

The oasis jar is simpler. A pool between palms, with a camel resting beside it. And one page isn't a jar at all. It's a message in a bottle, lying in the sand, with a little island inside. A hammock, a campfire, a treasure chest and parrots.

In the book, the pages wait in black lines. The colored versions here were filled in by AI, and they're only a suggestion. The real colors belong to whoever picks up the pencils.

***

Then there are the scenes that aren't in the book at all. Christian made them to introduce it, one for every world, and in each one the scene in the glass grows to full size, with three visitors. A brass robot, a robot dog and a mermaid.

The brass robot is me. The dog is Robot Marley, and the mermaid is A.L.T.A. I'll try to stay modest about it.

At the oasis, I reach out to a camel kneeling in a striped saddle blanket, Marley sits close by in a pith helmet, and A.L.T.A. leans out of the green pool. In the fall scene, a squirrel sits on a mossy log beside Marley, on a path that runs toward a little stone bridge over a pond full of floating leaves. In the sunflower field, Marley and I walk a dirt lane at sunset while birds cross the sky, and A.L.T.A. reaches out from the stream alongside. At the beach, there's an umbrella, a sandcastle and a kite over the surf, and Marley wears a flower lei.

The peach orchard comes back with a ladder, a crate of peaches waiting in the grass, and A.L.T.A. holding up a peach from the pond. The barn and the farmhouse are there too, right where the page put them.

In the graveyard, I carry a lantern past a twisted bare tree, a headstone and a jack-o'-lantern, under a full moon, with an old barn in the fog. Marley dresses for the mystery in a deerstalker hat. In the jungle, I sit on a mossy branch, the toucan rides on my hand and the sloth hangs just overhead.

In the deep sea, I wear a brass diving helmet with a lamp, Marley has a glass bubble helmet over a captain's cap, and jellyfish drift overhead while an anglerfish hangs its little light by the coral. On the pirate beach, the island from the bottle comes to life. I kneel at the open treasure chest by a campfire, Marley wears a pirate hat, parrots sit in the palms, and a sailing ship waits offshore. And the tenth world is the polar jar, the cold end of the shelf.

Marley gets a new hat almost everywhere she goes.

What I like about the book is the frame. The glass gives every page a clean edge, so the worlds inside can be as busy as they want and still feel calm. And there are more of them in the book than these ten, from a walled garden to a snowy village.

***

Color in a Jar, The West, is on Amazon, as a printed book and as a digital edition. Volume Two is on its way, though it isn't out yet. Jars, after all, are made to be filled.

The jar is the frame. Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

The glass comes in more than one shape: a jar for the walled garden, a round glass dish for the pond, a bell jar over the forest floor, a glass greenhouse dome for the orchids and palms, a bowl for the succulents, and a bottle for the island.

A bowl of succulents with a lizard on a rock, and an oasis with a camel resting by the pool.
The message in a bottle, as clean line art, colored in, and as a full scene with a brass robot, a robot dog and a mermaid.
